general.note: Buy regular rice flour, not glutinous rice flour.

tools.name: Saucepan
tools.note: Large size, used for cooking the grated radish.

tools.name: Cake pan
tools.note: Use an 8-inch square metal pan, since the cake is steamed in it.

tools.name: Pot
tools.note: Large, with a lid and a steamer rack that fits inside.

tools.name: Cooling rack
tools.note: A cooling rack lets the baked goods air out, but a plate or wire tray can stand in if you do not have one.

tools.name: Bowl
tools.note: A small bowl is enough for beating the eggs.

tools.name: Frying Pan
tools.note: A large nonstick frying pan is needed for frying the cake.

steps.title: Prep the ingredients
points: Prep everything first.
Peel the daikon and grate it on the coarse side of the box grater, keeping the juice.
In the mixing bowl, whisk the rice flour, 1 cup of the water, the salt, and the white pepper until smooth.
Grease the cake pan with 1 tablespoon of oil.
Mince the garlic.
Rinse the preserved radish, squeeze it dry, and chop it finely.
Beat the eggs with the fish sauce in the small bowl.
Slice the green onions.
Cover the frying ingredients and refrigerate them until you need them.

steps.title: Cook daikon and thicken paste
points: Put the grated daikon, its juice, and the remaining 1/2 cup of water in the large saucepan over medium heat.
Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until the radish is soft and translucent.
Turn the heat to low, whisk the flour mixture again, and pour it in.
Stir for 2 to 3 minutes until it forms a thick, heavy paste.
Take the pan off the heat and spread the paste evenly in the greased cake pan.

steps.title: Steam the cake
points: Set the steamer rack in the large pot and add water to 1 inch below the rack.
Bring it to a boil over high heat.
Set the cake pan on the rack, cover the pot, and turn the heat to medium.
Steam for 45 to 50 minutes, until the cake is firm and a skewer pushed into the center comes out clean.
Check the water every 15 minutes and top it up with boiling water from the kettle.

steps.title: Cool and cube the cake
points: Lift the cake pan out carefully and let it cool on the rack for 1 hour.
Refrigerate it for at least 3 hours, or overnight, until completely firm.
Turn the cake out onto the cutting board and cut it into 3/4-inch cubes.

steps.title: Brown the cubes
points: Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in the large nonstick frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add the cubes in a single layer and leave them alone for 4 to 5 minutes, until browned underneath.
Turn them and brown for another 3 to 4 minutes.

steps.title: Fry the aromatics
points: Push the cubes to one side of the pan.
Add the garlic and preserved radish to the cleared space and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Toss everything together and add the light soy sauce.

steps.title: Set and break the egg
points: Pour the egg mixture evenly over the cubes.
Let it set for 1 minute without stirring, then turn and break it into pieces with the spatula.
Cook for about 2 minutes more, until the egg is cooked through and lightly browned.
Scatter the green onions over, toss once, and serve hot.

troubleshooting.problem: The cake is too soft to cut and falls apart in the pan
troubleshooting.solution: Steam until the skewer comes out clean, and chill the cake overnight if you can.

troubleshooting.problem: The cubes stick and tear when you turn them
troubleshooting.solution: The oil was not hot enough, or the cubes were moved too soon. Wait for the oil to shimmer before adding the cubes, and do not turn them until a brown crust has formed.

troubleshooting.problem: The egg cooks into a separate scramble instead of coating the cubes
troubleshooting.solution: It was stirred too early. Pour it over the cubes and let it set for a full minute before breaking it up.
The preserved radish was not rinsed. Rinse and squeeze it well before chopping, and taste before adding any extra soy sauce.
